1.1: Adam had Seth, then came Enosh.
1.2: Enosh's fam kept it goin'—Cainan, Mahalalel, then Jared.
1.3: Jared had Enoch, who had Methuselah, then came Lamech.
1.4: Lamech had Noah. Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
1.5: Japheth's sons? Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
1.6: Gomer's sons: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
1.7: Javan's boys: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
1.8: Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
1.9: Cush had Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabtecha. Raamah had Sheba and Dedan.
1.10: Cush had Nimrod too. Bro started makin' a name for himself as a mighty dude on earth.
1.11: Mizraim had all these: Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
1.12: Pathrusim, Casluhim (Philistines came from them), and Caphtorim.
1.13: Canaan had Sidon, his firstborn, then Heth.
1.17: Shem had Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. Aram's sons: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
1.18: Arphaxad had Shelah, Shelah had Eber.
1.19: Eber had two boys—Peleg (named 'cause the earth got split up when he was born) and his brother Joktan.
1.20: Joktan had Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
1.23: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All them were Joktan's sons.
1.24: Here's the line: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,
1.27: Then came Abram—who later got renamed Abraham.
1.28: Abraham had two boys: Isaac and Ishmael.
1.29: Ishmael's sons: Nebajoth (the oldest), then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
1.31: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah—twelve sons in total.
1.32: Abraham's side woman, Keturah, had Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan had Sheba and Dedan.
1.33: Midian's sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All of them came from Keturah.
1.34: Isaac had Esau and Jacob (aka Israel).
1.35: Esau had Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah.
1.36: Eliphaz's boys: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, and Kenaz. Eliphaz and Timna had Amalek too.
1.37: Reuel's sons: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
1.38: Seir's sons: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
1.39: Lotan had Hori and Homam. His sister was Timna.
1.40: Shobal's sons: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon had Ajah and Anah.
1.41: Anah had Dishon. Dishon had Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
1.42: Ezer's sons: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan had Uz and Aran.
1.43: Before Israel had kings, Edom already had 'em. First up was Bela, son of Beor. His city? Dinhabah.
1.44: When Bela died, Jobab, son of Zerah from Bozrah, took over.
1.45: Then Jobab died, and Husham from Teman ruled next.
1.46: After Husham, Hadad son of Bedad took over. He's the one who beat Midian in Moab. His city? Avith.
1.47: Then came Samlah from Masrekah after Hadad passed.
1.48: After Samlah died, Saul from Rehoboth by the River stepped in.
1.49: Saul died, and Baal-Hanan, son of Achbor, ruled next.
1.50: Then Hadad took over. His city was Pai. His wife? Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, granddaughter of Mezahab.
1.51: Hadad died too. Then the chiefs of Edom were: Timnah, Aliah, Jetheth,
1.54: Magdiel, and Iram. Those were all the Edomite chiefs.

2.1: These was Jacob's sons—aka Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
2.2: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
2.3: Judah had three sons with a Canaanite woman named Shua's daughter—Er, Onan, and Shelah. But Er, the oldest, did some foul stuff in God's eyes, so God took him out.
2.4: Then Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, had twin boys by him—Perez and Zerah. So in total, Judah had five sons.
2.5: Perez had two sons: Hezron and Hamul.
2.6: Zerah had five: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara.
2.7: Carmi had a son named Achar—he the one who brought drama to Israel by takin' what was cursed.
2.8: Ethan had a son named Azariah.
2.9: Hezron's sons? Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
2.10: Ram had Amminadab, who had Nahshon—he was a big-time leader for Judah.
2.11: Nahshon had Salma, and Salma had Boaz.
2.12: Boaz had Obed, and Obed had Jesse.
2.13: Jesse's sons: Eliab was the first, Abinadab second, Shimea third,
2.15: Ozem sixth, and David was number seven.
2.16: Jesse also had daughters—Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's boys were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel—three solid warriors.
2.17: Abigail had a son named Amasa. His daddy was Jether, an Ishmaelite.
2.18: Caleb (Hezron's son) had kids by his wife Azubah and also Jerioth. Their sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
2.19: When Azubah passed, Caleb married Ephrath, and she had Hur.
2.20: Hur had Uri, and Uri had Bezalel.
2.21: Later, Hezron married Machir's daughter (that's Gilead's pops) when he was sixty. She gave birth to Segub.
2.22: Segub had Jair, who ended up with 23 towns in Gilead.
2.23: But Geshur and Aram snatched some of them towns from Jair—Kenath and its hood too. Sixty towns total. All of 'em was part of Machir's fam, Gilead's people.
2.24: When Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, his widow Abijah had Ashhur, who became the father of Tekoa.
2.25: Jerahmeel (Hezron's oldest) had these sons: Ram (the oldest), Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
2.26: He had another wife too, named Atarah. She was Onam's mama.
2.27: Ram's sons were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
2.28: Onam's boys were Shammai and Jada. Shammai had Nadab and Abishur.
2.29: Abishur's wife was Abihail. She had Ahban and Molid.
2.30: Nadab had Seled and Appaim. Seled didn't have no kids.
2.31: Appaim had Ishi, Ishi had Sheshan, and Sheshan had Ahlai.
2.32: Jada (Shammai's brother) had Jether and Jonathan. Jether didn't have kids.
2.33: Jonathan's sons were Peleth and Zaza. That's all Jerahmeel's people.
2.34: Now Sheshan ain't have no sons—just daughters. So he gave one of his daughters to his Egyptian servant Jarha.
2.35: They had a son named Attai.
2.36: Attai had Nathan, and Nathan had Zabad.
2.37: Zabad had Ephlal, and Ephlal had Obed.
2.38: Obed had Jehu, and Jehu had Azariah.
2.39: Azariah had Helez, and Helez had Eleasah.
2.40: Eleasah had Sismai, and Sismai had Shallum.
2.41: Shallum had Jekamiah, and Jekamiah had Elishama.
2.42: Caleb (Jerahmeel's brother) had a son named Mesha, who started Ziph's line. He also had Mareshah, father of Hebron.
2.43: Hebron's sons: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
2.44: Shema had Raham (father of Jorkoam), and Rekem had Shammai.
2.45: Shammai's son was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.
2.46: Caleb's side chick Ephah had Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran also had Gazez.
2.47: Jahdai had these sons: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
2.48: Another one of Caleb's side chicks, Maachah, had Sheber and Tirhanah.
2.49: She also gave birth to Shaaph (father of Madmannah), and Sheva (father of Machbenah and Gibea). Caleb also had a daughter named Achsah.
2.50: These were Caleb's descendants. Hur (Ephrathah's firstborn) had Shobal, father of Kirjath Jearim,
2.51: Salma, who started Bethlehem, and Hareph, who ran Beth Gader.
2.52: Shobal had sons too: Haroeh and half the fams of Manuhoth.
2.53: Kirjath Jearim had families like the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. From them came the Zorathites and Eshtaolites.
2.54: Salma's people were from Bethlehem, Netophah, Atroth Beth Joab, half the Manahethites, and the Zorites.
2.55: There was also a group of scribes livin' at Jabez—Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Suchathites. They were Kenites from Hammath, who came from Rechab's fam.

3.1: These the sons David had while he was livin' in Hebron: First was Amnon by Ahinoam from Jezreel. Second was Daniel by Abigail from Carmel.
3.2: Third was Absalom—his mama was Maacah, daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur. Fourth was Adonijah, son of Haggith.
3.3: Fifth was Shephatiah by Abital. Sixth was Ithream by his wife Eglah.
3.4: So six sons came while he was runnin' Hebron, where he ruled for seven years and six months. Then he moved to Jerusalem and reigned there thirty-three more years.
3.5: In Jerusalem, David had more kids: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon—those four came from Bathshua, daughter of Ammiel.
3.6: He also had Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet.
3.7: Then came Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia.
3.8: And Elishama again (yep, another one), Eliada, and another Eliphelet—nine sons total in Jerusalem.
3.9: These were all David's sons, not even countin' the ones from his side chicks. Tamar was their sister.
3.10: Solomon's son was Rehoboam. Then came Abijah, then Asa, then Jehoshaphat.
3.11: Jehoshaphat had Joram. Joram had Ahaziah. Ahaziah had Joash.
3.12: Joash had Amaziah, who had Azariah, who had Jotham.
3.13: Jotham had Ahaz, who had Hezekiah, who had Manasseh.
3.14: Manasseh had Amon, who had Josiah.
3.15: Josiah's sons were: Johanan (firstborn), Jehoiakim (second), Zedekiah (third), and Shallum (fourth).
3.16: Jehoiakim's sons were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.
3.18: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
3.19: Pedaiah had Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's kids were Meshullam, Hananiah, and their sister Shelomith.
3.20: Also: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed—five total.
3.21: Hananiah had Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. Then came the sons of Rephaiah, then Arnan, Obadiah, and Shechaniah.
3.22: Shechaniah had a son named Shemaiah. Shemaiah had Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat—six in all.
3.23: Neariah had Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam—three sons.
3.24: Elioenai had seven sons: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.

4.1: Judah had these sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
4.2: Shobal's son Reaiah had Jahath, who had Ahumai and Lahad. That whole crew was the fam of the Zorathites.
4.3: From the fam of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was Hazelelponi.
4.4: Penuel ran Gedor, and Ezer ran Hushah. These were Hur's people—he was Ephrathah's oldest son and the one who started Bethlehem's line.
4.5: Ashhur, the man from Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.
4.6: Naarah had Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. That was her squad.
4.7: Helah had Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan.
4.8: Koz had Anub, Zobebah, and the fam of Aharhel, Harum's son.
4.9: Now Jabez stood out from his brothers—his mama named him Jabez 'cause she had a hard labor.
4.10: Jabez prayed to the God of Israel sayin', 'Lord, bless me real good, stretch my territory, keep your hand on me, and don't let no evil cause me or others pain!' And God came through and granted his prayer.
4.11: Chelub, Shuhah's brother, had Mehir, who had Eshton.
4.12: Eshton's line included Beth-Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah (he ran Ir-Nahash). That whole crew came from Rechah.
4.13: Kenaz had Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel had Hathath,
4.14: and Meonothai had Ophrah. Seraiah had Joab, who ran Ge Harashim—place where all the craftsmen worked.
4.15: Caleb (Jephunneh's son) had Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.
4.16: Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
4.17: Ezrah had Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered's wife had Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah (who started Eshtemoa).
4.18: His other wife Jehudijah gave birth to Jered (who ran Gedor), Heber (who ran Sochoh), and Jekuthiel (who ran Zanoah). They all came from Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter—she married Mered.
4.19: Hodiah's wife, Naham's sister, had the leaders of Keilah (the Garmite) and Eshtemoa (the Maachathite).
4.20: Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's sons were Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.
4.21: Shelah, Judah's son, had Er (who ran Lecah), Laadah (who ran Mareshah), and the linen workers in Ashbea's house.
4.22: Also, Jokim, the men from Chozeba, Joash, Saraph (who ruled in Moab), and Jashubi-Lehem. That's old school history right there.
4.23: These were potters and craftsmen who stayed in Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king.
4.24: Simeon's sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
4.25: Shaul had Shallum, who had Mibsam, who had Mishma.
4.26: Mishma had Hamuel, Hamuel had Zacchur, Zacchur had Shimei.
4.27: Shimei had 16 sons and 6 daughters, but his brothers didn't have big families like Judah's folks.
4.28: They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, and Hazar Shual,
4.31: Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim. These were their cities up 'til David was king.
4.32: They also had villages: Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five more towns.
4.33: Plus all the little villages around them, stretchin' out toward Baal. They held it down there and kept their family records straight.
4.34: Some of the leaders were Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah (son of Amaziah),
4.35: Joel, and Jehu (son of Joshibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel),
4.36: Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah,
4.37: And Ziza (son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah). All these were big names in their clans, and their families multiplied like crazy.
4.38: These heads of families made moves and grew their clan real strong.
4.39: They rolled up to Gedor's entrance on the east side of the valley lookin' for good land to feed their flocks.
4.40: They found a big, peaceful, and fertile area—nice and quiet. The Hamites used to live there.
4.41: Back in King Hezekiah's day, some of these brothers attacked the tents and the Meunites there and wiped them out. They settled in and stayed 'cause the land had plenty of room for their livestock.
4.42: About 500 of them from Simeon's tribe went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel—sons of Ishi.
4.43: They defeated the last of the Amalekites who escaped, and they still livin' there to this day.

5.1: So Reuben was Israel's firstborn, but he messed up big time by sleepin' with his daddy's concubine. That move cost him the birthright—it got handed over to Joseph's sons. So when folks track the family tree, Reuben ain't listed first no more.
5.2: Judah ended up outshining all the brothers and even gave us a king. But technically, the birthright still belonged to Joseph's line.
5.3: Reuben's sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
5.4: Joel's line went like this: Shemaiah, then Gog, then Shimei,
5.6: and Beerah. Beerah was the leader of the Reubenites, but he got taken captive by Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria.
5.7: Here's a few more of Reuben's crew, recorded by family: Jeiel (the chief), Zechariah,
5.8: and Bela (son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel). They lived out in Aroer, stretched out all the way to Nebo and Baal Meon.
5.9: They spread even further east, toward the desert by the Euphrates, 'cause their livestock was deep and needed space.
5.10: Back when Saul was king, they went to war with the Hagrites, won that battle, and took over the land east of Gilead.
5.11: The tribe of Gad lived next door to Reuben's people in Bashan, reachin' all the way to Salcah.
5.12: Joel was their top guy, then Shapham, then Jaanai, then Shaphat—all in Bashan.
5.13: The rest of their family included Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber—seven total.
5.14: They came from Abihail, who came from Huri, who came from Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz. Real long line of folks.
5.15: Ahi (son of Abdiel, son of Guni) was the head of their clan.
5.16: Gad's people stayed in Gilead, in Bashan, in the villages around there, and even in the open lands of Sharon.
5.17: All these folks got recorded in the family books back when Jotham ruled Judah and Jeroboam ruled Israel.
5.18: The Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh's tribe had 44,760 warriors—ready for action with shields, swords, bows, and skills.
5.19: They went to war with the Hagrites and their people—Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
5.20: God had their back. They cried out to Him during battle, and He came through. They trusted Him, and He delivered the win.
5.21: They took a crazy amount of livestock: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys—and even captured 100,000 people.
5.22: It was a big win, and a lot of folks died, 'cause the war wasn't just theirs—it was God's. They stayed in that land 'til they got taken into exile.
5.23: The half-tribe of Manasseh lived from Bashan all the way to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon. Their numbers grew heavy.
5.24: The leaders of their families were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—straight-up warriors, well-known, and respected in their bloodlines.
5.25: But they started wildin'—turnin' their backs on the God of their ancestors. They started messin' around with other gods, like the same ones God had kicked out the land.
5.26: So God stirred up the spirit of Pul (aka Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria), and he came for 'em. He took the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh into exile—to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan. And that's where they still at to this day.

6.1: Levi had three sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
6.2: Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
6.3: Amram had Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
6.4: Eleazar had Phinehas, and Phinehas had Abishua.
6.5: Abishua had Bukki, and Bukki had Uzzi.
6.6: Uzzi had Zerahiah, and Zerahiah had Meraioth.
6.7: Meraioth had Amariah, and Amariah had Ahitub.
6.8: Ahitub had Zadok, and Zadok had Ahimaaz.
6.9: Ahimaaz had Azariah, and Azariah had Johanan.
6.10: Johanan had another Azariah—he the one who was priest when Solomon's temple got built in Jerusalem.
6.11: That Azariah had Amariah, and Amariah had Ahitub.
6.12: Ahitub had another Zadok, and that Zadok had Shallum.
6.13: Shallum had Hilkiah, and Hilkiah had another Azariah.
6.14: Azariah had Seraiah, and Seraiah had Jehozadak.
6.15: Jehozadak got taken away into exile when the Lord let Judah and Jerusalem fall into Babylon's hands under Nebuchadnezzar.
6.16: Levi's sons? Still the same three: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
6.17: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
6.18: Kohath's sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
6.19: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. That's how the Levite families broke down by their daddies.
6.20: From Gershon's line: Libni, then Jahath, then Zimmah,
6.21: then Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai.
6.22: Kohath's line: Amminadab, then Korah, then Assir,
6.24: then Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.
6.26: Then Elkanah's line kept goin': Zophai, Nahath,
6.27: then Eliab, Jeroham, and another Elkanah.
6.28: Samuel's sons: Joel (his oldest) and Abijah (his second).
6.29: Merari's line: Mahli, then Libni, then Shimei, then Uzzah,
6.31: These the men King David picked to lead the worship music after the Ark got settled.
6.32: They handled all the music at the tent of meeting before Solomon built the temple in Jerusalem. They kept doin' their duty just like they were assigned.
6.33: From the Kohathites came Heman the singer. He was the son of Joel, who was the son of Samuel,
6.34: son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,
6.35: son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,
6.36: son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
6.37: son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
6.38: son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
6.39: Standin' to his right was his brother Asaph. He was the son of Berachiah, son of Shimea,
6.40: son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah.
6.41: Ethni's son was Zerah, Zerah's son was Adaiah.
6.42: Adaiah had Ethan, Ethan had Zimmah, Zimmah had Shimei.
6.43: Shimei had Jahath, Jahath had Gershon, and Gershon was Levi's son.
6.44: Merari's fam held it down on the left side. That included Ethan, son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,
6.45: son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,
6.46: son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shamer,
6.47: son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
6.48: All the other Levite brothers handled everything else in the temple—they were assigned to all kinds of jobs in the house of God.
6.49: Aaron and his sons did the sacrifices—burnt offerings, incense offerings, and all the atonement work in the Most Holy Place, just like God told Moses to set it up.
6.50: Aaron's line was: Eleazar, then Phinehas, then Abishua,
6.51: then Bukki, then Uzzi, then Zerahiah,
6.52: then Meraioth, then Amariah, then Ahitub,
6.54: These are the places the Levites got to live, handed out by tribe and family. The sons of Aaron (from Kohath's crew) got their land by lot.
6.55: They gave 'em Hebron in Judah, along with the land around it.
6.56: But the fields and villages nearby? Those went to Caleb, son of Jephunneh.
6.57: Aaron's folks got one of the cities of refuge—Hebron. Plus Libnah, Jattir, and Eshtemoa, all with land around 'em.
6.59: Ashan, and Beth Shemesh—all with their common-lands too.
6.60: From Benjamin's tribe, they got Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth. That made thirteen cities total for Aaron's fam.
6.61: The rest of Kohath's people got ten cities from half the tribe of Manasseh.
6.62: The Gershonites got thirteen cities spread across Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the Manasseh territory in Bashan.
6.63: Merari's descendants got twelve cities from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
6.64: The Israelites gave all these cities, along with surrounding lands, to the Levites.
6.65: The Levites got these cities by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin—each named specifically.
6.66: Some of Kohath's descendants got cities in Ephraim's territory.
6.67: They gave them Shechem (a city of refuge) in the hill country of Ephraim, plus Gezer,
6.69: Aijalon, and Gath Rimmon—all with common-lands.
6.70: From half of Manasseh's tribe, they got Aner and Bileam.
6.71: Gershon's line, from that same half-tribe of Manasseh, got Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth.
6.76: From Naphtali's tribe: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kirjathaim.
6.77: From Zebulun's tribe, Merari's remaining fam got Rimmon and Tabor.
6.78: On the east side of the Jordan (across from Jericho), they got land from Reuben's tribe: Bezer in the wilderness, Jahzah,
6.80: From Gad's tribe, they got Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim,
6.81: Heshbon, and Jazer—all with their common-lands.

7.1: Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.
7.2: Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam, and Shemuel. These were the heads of their daddy's clan—straight warriors. Back in King David's time, Tola's line had 22,600 soldiers deep.
7.3: Uzzi's son was Izrahiah, and Izrahiah had five sons: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah. All of them were leaders.
7.4: Alongside them, their clan had 36,000 soldiers ready for war—'cause they had plenty of wives and kids.
7.5: Across all Issachar's fams, they had 87,000 strong warriors, all recorded by name.
7.6: Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
7.7: Bela's boys were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri—five total. They led their clans and had 22,034 warriors recorded.
7.8: Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.
7.9: They were listed as heads of their houses—20,200 mighty soldiers.
7.10: Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tharshish, and Ahishahar.
7.11: All of Jediael's boys led their clans too—17,200 warriors, ready for battle.
7.12: Shuppim and Huppim were Ir's sons, and Hushim was Aher's son.
7.13: Naphtali had four sons: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were Bilhah's kids.
7.14: Manasseh had kids through a side chick from Syria. She had Machir (father of Gilead), who had Asriel.
7.15: Machir married Maachah (she was Huppim and Shuppim's sister). Gilead's grandson was Zelophehad—he only had daughters.
7.16: Maachah had another son named Peresh. His brother was Sheresh. Sheresh's sons were Ulam and Rakem.
7.17: Ulam's son was Bedan. That whole crew came down from Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh.
7.18: Hammoleketh (Gilead's sister) had Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
7.19: Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
7.20: Ephraim had Shuthelah, who had Bered, who had Tahath, who had Eladah, who had another Tahath,
7.21: who had Zabad, who had another Shuthelah. Ezer and Elead—sons of Ephraim—got killed by some men from Gath 'cause they tried to jack their livestock.
7.22: Ephraim was tore up about it and mourned for days. His brothers came to comfort him.
7.23: Then he laid with his wife, and she had a son. He named him Beriah, 'cause that tragedy hit their house hard.
7.24: His daughter Sheerah built Lower and Upper Beth Horon, and Uzzen Sheerah.
7.25: His line continued with Rephah, Resheph, Telah, Tahan,
7.28: They lived in Bethel and its nearby towns. Eastward was Naaran, westward was Gezer and its towns. Also Shechem and Ayyah with their towns.
7.29: Along the edge of Manasseh's border were Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor—all with their towns. Joseph's descendants held down all that land.
7.30: Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah.
7.31: Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel—Malchiel started Birzaith.
7.32: Heber had Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.
7.33: Japhlet's sons: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.
7.34: Shemer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
7.35: Helem's sons (Shemer's brother) were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
7.36: Zophah's sons: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, and Imrah.
7.37: Also Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Jithran, and Beera.
7.38: Jether's sons: Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.
7.39: Ulla's sons: Arah, Haniel, and Rizia.
7.40: All these were Asher's descendants—heads of their clans, respected men, warriors, and top leaders. They were registered as battle-ready soldiers—26,000 in total.

8.1: Benjamin had five sons: Bela was his first, Ashbel second, Aharah third,
8.2: Nohah was fourth, and Rapha was fifth.
8.3: Bela's sons were Addar, Gera, Abihud,
8.6: These were the sons of Ehud. They ran their father's households in Geba and ended up movin' folks to Manahath.
8.7: Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera made that move happen. Gera had Uzza and Ahihud.
8.8: Shaharaim had some kids while he was livin' in Moab. This was after he sent away his wives Hushim and Baara.
8.9: His wife Hodesh had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
8.10: Jeuz, Sachiah, and Mirmah. All of 'em were heads of their fams.
8.11: With Hushim, he had Abitub and Elpaal.
8.12: Elpaal's sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed—he the one who built Ono and Lod with its towns.
8.13: Then there were Beriah and Shema. They ran the families in Aijalon and even kicked the Gath people out.
8.14: Other sons of Beriah: Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth,
8.17: Elpaal's other sons were Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
8.19: Shimei's sons were Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
8.22: Shashak's line had Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
8.26: Jeroham's sons were Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
8.28: These were all chiefs—heads of their clans, leaders in their day—and they lived in Jerusalem.
8.29: The man from Gibeon lived in Gibeon, and his wife was Maacah.
8.30: His oldest was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
8.32: and Mikloth, who had a son named Shimeah. They lived near their family in Jerusalem.
8.33: Ner had Kish. Kish had Saul. Saul had Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.
8.34: Jonathan had Merib-Baal, and Merib-Baal had Micah.
8.35: Micah had Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
8.36: Ahaz had Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah had Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri had Moza.
8.37: Moza had Binea, Binea had Raphah, Raphah had Eleasah, and Eleasah had Azel.
8.38: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All them were Azel's boys.
8.39: Azel's brother Eshek had sons too: Ulam (firstborn), Jeush (second), and Eliphelet (third).
8.40: Ulam's sons were straight-up warriors—archers with mad skills. He had a big family: 150 sons and grandsons. All of them were from Benjamin's tribe.

9.1: All of Israel got written down in the family records, and those records got kept in the Book of the Kings of Israel. But Judah? They got sent into exile in Babylon 'cause they wasn't faithful to God.
9.2: The first folks to settle back in their cities and land were Israelites, priests, Levites, and the temple workers called the Nethinim.
9.3: Some of the folks from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.
9.4: Like Uthai, son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani—he came from Perez, Judah's son.
9.5: Then from the Shilonites, Asaiah the firstborn and his sons lived there.
9.6: From Zerah's line: Jeuel and 690 of his kin.
9.7: From Benjamin's line: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah.
9.8: Also Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.
9.9: All of them together—956 men, heads of their families.
9.10: The priests included Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.
9.11: Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub—he was the chief in charge of God's house.
9.12: Then Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer.
9.13: Their crew had 1,760 heads of households—real solid, capable men workin' the Lord's house.
9.14: From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah—from Merari's line.
9.15: Also Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Micah, son of Zichri, son of Asaph.
9.16: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah—he lived among the Netophathite villages.
9.17: Gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their fam—Shallum was the leader.
9.18: Back then, they stood watch at the King's Gate on the east side—Levi's folks handled that job.
9.19: Shallum, son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his family were in charge of guarding the temple entrances—same job their ancestors had back in the day.
9.20: Phinehas, Eleazar's son, had led them in the past—and the Lord had his back.
9.21: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah watched the door of the tabernacle.
9.22: All 212 gatekeepers got recorded in the family books. King David and the prophet Samuel had put them in these trusted positions.
9.23: They and their kids had shifts guarding the Lord's house—the tabernacle doors.
9.24: Gatekeepers were posted in all four directions: east, west, north, and south.
9.25: Their cousins from the villages came through every seven days to take shifts.
9.26: There were four chief gatekeepers—Levites—who had charge over the storage rooms and treasuries of the temple.
9.27: They lived all around God's house, 'cause they were responsible for it and had to unlock the doors each morning.
9.28: Some Levites were in charge of the sacred vessels—they kept count when bringing them in and takin' them out.
9.29: Others handled the furniture, all the temple gear, the flour, wine, oil, incense, and spices.
9.30: Some of the priests even made the special mix for the incense.
9.31: Mattithiah, Shallum's firstborn from the Korahite line, was in charge of what got baked in the pans.
9.32: Some of their Kohathite brothers handled the showbread every Sabbath.
9.33: The singers—heads of the Levite families—lived in the temple rooms. They were on duty day and night and didn't have to do anything else.
9.34: These heads of Levite families were leaders in their time. They lived in Jerusalem.
9.35: Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife's name was Maacah.
9.36: His oldest son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
9.38: Mikloth had Shimeam. They all lived near their fam in Jerusalem.
9.39: Ner had Kish, Kish had Saul, and Saul had Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.
9.40: Jonathan's son was Merib-Baal, and he had a son named Micah.
9.41: Micah's sons: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
9.42: Ahaz had Jarah. Jarah had Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri had Moza.
9.43: Moza had Binea, who had Rephaiah, who had Eleasah, who had Azel.
9.44: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. That's Azel's whole squad.

10.1: The Philistines went to war with Israel, and Israelite soldiers got shook and ran. A bunch of them got killed up on Mount Gilboa.
10.2: The Philistines kept chasin' Saul and his sons. They ended up killin' Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua—Saul's boys.
10.3: The fight was gettin' real heavy around Saul. The archers spotted him, lit him up with arrows, and he got wounded bad.
10.4: Saul told his armorbearer, 'Man, pull out your sword and finish me off before these uncircumcised dudes come through and humiliate me.' But his armorbearer was too scared—he couldn't do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
10.5: When the armorbearer saw Saul was dead, he did the same—fell on his own sword too.
10.6: That's how Saul, his three sons, and everybody in his household died that day—all gone together.
10.7: When the rest of Israel saw what happened—how Saul and his sons were gone—they dipped. They left their towns, and the Philistines moved right in.
10.8: Next day, the Philistines came back to loot the battlefield and found Saul and his sons laid out on Mount Gilboa.
10.9: They stripped Saul's body, took his head and armor, and sent the news all around Philistia—braggin' in their idol temples and to the public.
10.10: They put Saul's armor in their god's temple and stuck his head up in Dagon's temple like a trophy.
10.11: When the folks from Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines did to Saul,
10.12: all their brave men got up, grabbed Saul's body and his sons' bodies, brought them back to Jabesh, buried their bones under a tamarisk tree, and fasted for seven days.
10.13: Saul died 'cause he was unfaithful to the Lord. He didn't do what God said, and even went to a psychic for advice.
10.14: He ain't go to God for direction, so God took him out and handed the kingdom over to David, Jesse's son.

11.1: All of Israel pulled up to Hebron and told David, 'You fam. You one of us—flesh and bone.'
11.2: 'Even back when Saul was king, you were really the one leadin' us out to battle and bringin' us back. The Lord your God already said, "You gon' be the shepherd of My people and rule over Israel."'
11.3: So the elders of Israel came to David at Hebron, and David made a pact with them before God. Then they anointed him king, just like the Lord had said through Samuel.
11.4: David and all of Israel rolled up on Jerusalem (back then it was called Jebus). The Jebusites still lived there.
11.5: The Jebusites told David, 'You ain't gettin' in here!' But David wasn't hearing it—he took the stronghold of Zion anyway. That's what they started callin' the City of David.
11.6: David said, 'Whoever hits them Jebusites first gon' be my right-hand man.' Joab, son of Zeruiah, stepped up first—and boom—he got promoted.
11.7: David moved into that stronghold, and they named it the City of David.
11.8: He built up the whole area around it—from the Millo outward. Joab helped rebuild the rest.
11.9: And David kept leveling up. The Lord of Heaven's Armies was with him.
11.10: These were the top warriors David had—the ones who stood with him strong while he was getting established as king. They helped lock it in, just like God promised.
11.11: Jashobeam, son of a Hachmonite, was head of the captains. He lifted his spear and took out 300 men all by himself—one swing, one moment.
11.12: Next up was Eleazar, son of Dodo the Ahohite—one of the big three.
11.13: He rode with David at Pasdammim when the Philistines pulled up to fight in a barley field. Everybody else dipped.
11.14: But he and David stood their ground right in the middle of that field, held it down, and dropped Philistines left and right. God came through with a major W.
11.15: Three of the top 30 leaders came to David at the rock near the cave of Adullam while the Philistines had set up camp in the Valley of Rephaim.
11.16: David was holed up in a stronghold, and the Philistines had soldiers occupying Bethlehem.
11.17: David, real thirsty, said, 'Man, I wish somebody could get me a sip from that well near the gate of Bethlehem.'
11.18: So the three of them broke through the Philistine lines, got water from that well, and brought it back. But David wouldn't even drink it—he poured it out to the Lord.
11.19: He said, 'I can't drink this—it's like drinkin' the blood of the homies who risked their lives to get it.' So he offered it to God instead. That's the kinda stuff these three mighty men were on.
11.20: Abishai, Joab's brother, led another group of three. He took out 300 men with his spear and earned mad respect.
11.21: He was the most honored among that crew and became their captain—but he still didn't top the original three.
11.22: Then there was Benaiah, son of Jehoiada—from Kabzeel. Dude was built different. Took out two warrior-beasts from Moab, chased down a lion in a snowy pit and killed it.
11.23: He even killed an Egyptian giant, like 7½ feet tall. The man had a spear like a beam. Benaiah came at him with a stick, snatched the spear, and ended him with his own weapon.
11.24: Benaiah made a name for himself with those moves—he stood out.
11.25: He was more honored than the thirty but didn't make the cut for the original three. Still, David put him over his security detail.
11.26: Here's more of David's real ones: Asahel (Joab's brother), Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
11.27: Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
11.28: Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa, Abiezer from Anathoth,
11.29: Sibbechai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
11.30: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah from Netophath,
11.31: Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
11.32: Hurai from Gaash Valley, Abiel the Arbathite,
11.33: Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
11.34: Sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shageh the Hararite,
11.35: Ahiam son of Sacar from Harar, Eliphal son of Ur,
11.36: Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,
11.37: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai,
11.38: Joel, Nathan's brother, Mibhar son of Hagri,
11.39: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite—Joab's armorbearer,
11.40: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
11.41: Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai,
11.42: Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, chief of the Reubenites—he had thirty with him,
11.43: Hanan son of Maachah, Joshaphat the Mithnite,
11.44: Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel sons of Hotham the Aroerite,
11.45: Jediael son of Shimri, and his brother Joha the Tizite,
11.46: Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite,
11.47: Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

12.1: These the real ones who came through to Ziklag to roll with David, back when he was still duckin' Saul. These dudes? Straight warriors, ready to throw hands.
12.2: They could shoot arrows or sling stones with either hand—ambidextrous snipers from the tribe of Benjamin, Saul's own fam.
12.3: The main ones was Ahiezer and Joash, sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. Then there was Jeziel, Pelet (Azmaveth's sons), Berachah, and Jehu from Anathoth.
12.4: Ishmaiah from Gibeon was a beast—one of the top 30, and even led them. Then you got Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad from Gederath.
12.5: Also Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah from Haruph.
12.6: Then came Elkanah, Jisshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam—all from the Korah fam.
12.7: Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor, pulled up too.
12.8: Some cold-blooded warriors from Gad rolled up on David in the wilderness. These ain't your average dudes—trained to fight, hold a shield, toss a spear, and they looked like lions in the face. They was fast too, like mountain deer.
12.9: Ezer was the top dawg, then Obadiah second, Eliab third,
12.14: All them from Gad, some real-deal captains—smallest one could command a hundred, the biggest? A thousand deep.
12.15: They even crossed the Jordan when the water was wild, flooded and all. Didn't matter—they cleared out whole valleys, east and west, no hesitation.
12.16: Some dudes from Benjamin and Judah came through to link up with David at the stronghold.
12.17: David stepped out to meet them like, 'Aight, if y'all here in peace to ride with me, cool, we good. But if y'all schemin' on me, just know I ain't done nobody dirty, and may God judge if y'all on some betrayal type stuff.'
12.18: Then the Spirit hit Amasai, the lead captain, and he said, 'We with you, David! All in, son of Jesse! Peace to you and your folks—'cause your God got your back.' So David welcomed 'em and made 'em squad captains.
12.19: Some cats from Manasseh dipped out on Saul and came to David too. This was when David almost rode with the Philistines but they didn't trust him, thinking he'd flip and help Saul instead.
12.20: When David got back to Ziklag, the ones from Manasseh who joined him were Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, another Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai—big dawgs, all leading thousands.
12.21: They helped David fight off raiders. These men? Straight warriors, leaders in the battlefield.
12.22: And day by day, more folks kept comin' to help David 'til his army started lookin' like God's own squad—deep and powerful.
12.23: Here's the headcount of troops that came to Hebron to hand the kingdom over to David, just like The Most High said it would go down:
12.24: Judah had 6,800 warriors, strapped with shield and spear.
12.25: Simeon brought 7,100 real ones—fit for war.
12.27: With them was Jehoiada, reppin' Aaron's line, with 3,700 soldiers.
12.28: Zadok was there too—young and fierce—and brought 22 leaders from his fam.
12.29: Benjamin, Saul's people, had 3,000. Most of them had still been loyal to Saul's house, but some came through.
12.30: Ephraim showed up 20,800 deep—famous for being brave and strong.
12.31: Half-tribe of Manasseh brought 18,000, already chosen to help crown David.
12.32: Issachar's crew was sharp—they understood the times and knew what Israel needed to do. They had 200 leaders, and their people followed their lead.
12.33: Zebulun had 50,000 seasoned warriors, ready for anything. They ain't fold, stayed in formation.
12.34: Naphtali came with 1,000 captains and 37,000 soldiers with shields and spears.
12.35: Dan brought 28,600 who could move like a unit.
12.36: Asher had 40,000 who could go to war and hold formation.
12.37: From across the Jordan—Reuben, Gad, and the other half of Manasseh came strapped with all kinds of weapons—120,000 strong.
12.38: All these warriors rolled into Hebron with loyal hearts, ready to make David king over all Israel. The whole nation was united behind this move.
12.39: They stayed with David three whole days, feasting and chillin'. Their brothers had already set the table.
12.40: Folks came from as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, bringin' food stacked on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen—flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, beef, and sheep. It was a whole celebration—Israel was straight-up joyful.

13.1: David called a meeting with all his top soldiers—thousands, hundreds—and every other leader too.
13.2: Then he told everybody in Israel, 'Aight y'all, if this sound good to y'all and God co-sign it, let's hit up all our people still scattered across the land, plus the priests and Levites chillin' in their towns and fields. Tell 'em to link up with us.'
13.3: 'We need to bring God's Ark back home. We ain't even prayed in front of it since Saul was king.'
13.4: Everybody was like, 'Bet. Let's do it.' Sounded right to the whole crew.
13.5: So David gathered everybody from all over—far as Egypt to the edge of Hamath—to go get the Ark of God from Kirjath Jearim.
13.6: David and all Israel went up to Baalah (aka Kirjath Jearim) in Judah to bring back the Ark of God—the one that's posted between the cherubim, where His name stay holy.
13.7: They put the Ark on a brand-new cart, straight from Abinadab's house. Uzza and Ahio were drivin' that cart.
13.8: David and the whole squad started turnin' up in front of God—singin', goin' in with harps, strings, tambourines, cymbals, and blowin' them trumpets like it was a full-on praise party.
13.9: But when they pulled up near Chidon's threshing floor, the oxen tripped, and Uzza reached out to steady the Ark.
13.10: God got hot real quick. He wasn't playin' about His Ark—struck Uzza down right there for touchin' it. Uzza died on the spot, in front of God.
13.11: David got mad—like real mad—'cause God snapped on Uzza like that. That place been called Perez Uzza ever since, meanin' 'God's outburst on Uzza.'
13.12: David started feelin' some type of way about God that day. He was shook and said, 'How I'm supposed to bring the Ark to my crib now?'
13.13: So David ain't take the Ark into his city. Instead, he had it dropped off at Obed-Edom the Gittite's house.
13.14: The Ark stayed at Obed-Edom's place for three whole months—and God poured out blessings on his whole household and everything he owned.

14.1: Hiram, king of Tyre, hit David up—sent messengers with cedar wood, builders, and carpenters to build him a crib.
14.2: That's when David knew, for real for real, that the Lord had set him up as king over Israel. His kingdom was glowin' up, all 'cause God was lookin' out for His people.
14.3: David got himself some more wives while livin' in Jerusalem, and he had more sons and daughters too.
14.4: Here go the names of the kids he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,
14.8: Now when the Philistines heard David was crowned king over all Israel, they pulled up tryin' to catch him slippin'. But David got word and stepped out to meet 'em head-on.
14.9: The Philistines ran up on the Valley of Rephaim, ready to raid.
14.10: David went to God, like, 'Should I go fight 'em? You gon' hand 'em over to me?' And God said, 'Go ahead—I got you. You gon' win this.'
14.11: So they met up at Baal Perazim, and David wrecked 'em there. He said, 'God broke through my enemies like a flood bustin' through!' That's why they called that spot Baal Perazim.
14.12: The Philistines left their fake gods behind when they dipped, and David told his people, 'Burn all that up. We don't need it.' So they torched it.
14.13: But the Philistines came back again, same valley, lookin' for smoke.
14.14: David went to God again, and this time God said, 'Nah, don't hit 'em head-on. Swing around back and wait by the mulberry trees.'
14.15: 'When you hear footsteps movin' through the tops of those trees, that's your cue. Jump out then, 'cause that's Me goin' ahead of you, takin' out the Philistine camp.'
14.16: David followed the play God gave him, and they chased them Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer. They didn't stand a chance.
14.17: After that, David's name rang out everywhere. And the Lord made sure everybody in every nation was shook when they heard his name.

15.1: David built himself some cribs in the City of David. He also set up a special spot—a tent—just for God's Ark.
15.2: Then David said, 'Only the Levites can carry God's Ark. That's who the Lord picked to handle it and serve Him forever.'
15.3: So David called the whole nation to pull up to Jerusalem so they could bring God's Ark to the place he set up.
15.4: Then David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:
15.5: From Kohath's crew: Uriel was the chief, with 120 of his folks.
15.7: From Gershom's line: Joel had 130 rollin' with him.
15.8: Elizaphan's squad came with Shemaiah leading 200.
15.9: Hebron's family brought 80, with Eliel in charge.
15.10: And Uzziel's people had Amminadab at the front, with 112 behind him.
15.11: David called up Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and them Levite leaders: Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
15.12: He told 'em, 'Y'all the heads of the Levite fams. You and your crew gotta purify yourselves, 'cause y'all gon' carry God's Ark to the place I prepped for it.'
15.13: 'Last time we ain't do it right—didn't ask God how to move, and He popped off on us for it.'
15.14: So the priests and Levites got themselves spiritually right to carry the Ark of the Lord God of Israel.
15.15: And just like Moses said, they lifted that Ark up on their shoulders with the poles, doin' it God's way this time.
15.16: David told the Levite leaders, 'Pick out folks to sing and play music—stringed instruments, harps, cymbals—let's make this a joyful noise for real.'
15.17: So the Levites chose Heman (Joel's son), Asaph (son of Berechiah), and Ethan (from Merari's line, son of Kushaiah).
15.18: They also brought in the second string crew: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, plus Obed-Edom and Jeiel as gatekeepers.
15.19: The main singers—Heman, Asaph, and Ethan—were the ones bangin' cymbals made of bronze.
15.20: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played strings, tuned to Alamoth style.
15.21: Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were on harps, tuned to Sheminith style.
15.22: Chenaniah, a Levite leader, was in charge of the music 'cause he was gifted like that.
15.23: Berechiah and Elkanah worked the doors where the Ark was.
15.24: Priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew trumpets in front of the Ark. Obed-Edom and Jehiah stayed on doorkeepin' duty.
15.25: David, the elders, and the commanders brought the Ark of the covenant of the Lord up from Obed-Edom's crib, and they were hyped.
15.26: When God helped the Levites carry the Ark, they showed love back—offered seven bulls and seven rams.
15.27: David was rockin' a fine linen robe, just like the Levites, the singers, and Chenaniah the music director. David also had on a linen ephod over it.
15.28: All Israel turned up as they brought the Ark back—shoutin', blowin' horns, blastin' trumpets, crashin' cymbals, and strummin' strings and harps.
15.29: But when the Ark got to the City of David, Michal (Saul's daughter) looked out the window, saw King David dancin' like he ain't care who was watchin'—and she felt some type of way. She was straight-up salty in her heart.

16.1: They brought the Ark of God and set it right in the tent David had pitched just for it. Then they gave burnt offerings and peace offerings in front of the Lord.
16.2: When David finished givin' those offerings, he turned to the people and blessed them in God's name.
16.3: Then he passed out food to everybody in Israel—man and woman. Each person got a loaf of bread, a piece of meat, and a cake made with raisins.
16.4: David picked out some Levites to stay on post in front of the Ark—to remember what God had done, to thank Him, and to praise Him.
16.5: Asaph was lead, then Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, and Obed-Edom. Jeiel was on the strings and harps, while Asaph handled the cymbals.
16.6: Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests kept blowin' them trumpets in front of the Ark like clockwork.
16.7: That same day, David handed over this praise song to Asaph and his crew to lead the people in thankin' the Lord:
16.8: 'Give thanks to the Lord! Call on His name! Let everybody know what He's done!'
16.9: 'Sing to Him, lift Him up in your songs. Talk about all His wild and wonderful works.'
16.10: 'Shout out His holy name! Let everybody who's really seekin' God be filled with joy!'
16.11: 'Go lookin' for the Lord and His strength. Don't stop chasin' after His presence!'
16.12: 'Remember all the things He done—His miracles and judgments He laid down.'
16.13: 'Y'all, the children of Israel—His chosen folks, Jacob's fam—don't forget who y'all belong to.'
16.14: 'He the Lord our God, and His judgment reaches across the earth.'
16.15: 'Never forget His covenant—His word stands for a thousand generations.'
16.16: 'The same one He gave Abraham, confirmed it with Isaac,'
16.17: 'And then made it law with Jacob—an eternal promise to Israel.'
16.18: 'He said, "I'ma give y'all the land of Canaan. That's your inheritance, your legacy."'
16.19: 'Even when y'all were just a few folks, wanderin' strangers in that land,'
16.20: 'Bouncin' from country to country, livin' as outsiders,'
16.21: 'God didn't let nobody mess with 'em. He even checked kings to protect His people,'
16.22: 'Sayin', "Don't lay a finger on My chosen ones. Don't harm My prophets."'
16.23: 'Sing to the Lord, whole world! Spread the word—salvation's here and it's daily!'
16.24: 'Tell every nation how glorious He is. Brag on His miracles everywhere.'
16.25: 'The Lord is great and deserves all the praise. Ain't no god above Him.'
16.26: 'Other so-called gods? Just idols. But the Lord? He made the whole universe.'
16.27: 'He got honor and majesty with Him—power and joy live where He is.'
16.28: 'Come on, families of the world—give God the glory He deserves. Show Him His strength.'
16.29: 'Give God the praise due His name. Bring Him an offering and come with respect. Worship Him in the beauty of holiness.'
16.30: 'Shake in His presence, whole earth. The world ain't goin' nowhere—it's locked in place.'
16.31: 'Let the skies turn up, and the earth celebrate! Let the nations say loud: "The Lord runs this!"'
16.32: 'Let the ocean roar and everything in it. Let the fields turn up too—all creation join in.'
16.33: 'Even the trees gon' clap for joy when the Lord shows up—to judge the earth right.'
16.34: 'Give thanks to the Lord, 'cause He's good. His mercy don't ever quit.'
16.35: 'And say this: "Save us, God! You the one who rescues. Bring us back and set us free from these other folks so we can shout thanks to Your name and celebrate Your praise."'
16.36: 'Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, forever and ever!' And everybody said, 'Amen!' and praised the Lord like they meant it.
16.37: David left Asaph and his crew right there in front of the Ark, to keep that worship goin' every day like clockwork.
16.38: Obed-Edom and his 68 fam members were also posted up, includin' his son Jeduthun and Hosah—they handled the gates.
16.39: Zadok the priest and his crew were posted at the Lord's tabernacle up in Gibeon.
16.40: They stayed offerin' burnt offerings every morning and night, just like the Law of the Lord told Israel to do.
16.41: Heman, Jeduthun, and the other chosen ones by name stayed on thanksgiving duty—praising God 'cause His mercy never runs out.
16.42: They had trumpets, cymbals, and all kinds of instruments dedicated to God. Even Jeduthun's sons were out there doin' gate duty.
16.43: Then everybody went home. David went back too—ready to bless his own house.

17.1: One day, while David was chillin' in his crib, he told the prophet Nathan, 'Man, look—I'm out here livin' in this fine cedar house, and God's Ark still sittin' out in a tent.'
17.2: Nathan told him, 'Do what's in your heart, bro. God's got you.'
17.3: But that night, God came to Nathan with a word.
17.4: He said, 'Go tell My servant David, "The Lord says: You ain't the one to build Me a house to live in."'
17.5: 'I ain't lived in no house since I brought Israel out of Egypt. I been movin' from tent to tent, tabernacle to tabernacle.'
17.6: 'Everywhere I've traveled with My people, did I ever tell any of the judges I set up over Israel, "Why ain't y'all built Me a house made of cedar?" Nope.'
17.7: 'So now, tell David this: "The Lord of Heaven's Armies says, I pulled you up from herdin' sheep to lead My people Israel.'
17.8: 'I been with you every step of the way, takin' out all your enemies. I done gave you a name—one that stand strong like the greatest names on earth.'
17.9: 'I'm finna lock in a spot for My people Israel—a place they can call home, no more bouncin' around. No more evil folks runnin' up on 'em like before.'
17.10: 'Ever since I raised up judges, it's been chaos, but I'ma calm all your enemies down. And check this—I'ma build YOU a house.'
17.11: 'When your time's up, and you rest with your ancestors, I'ma raise up one of your sons after you. I'ma make his kingdom solid.'
17.12: 'He the one who's gon' build Me a house. And I'ma lock his throne down forever.'
17.13: 'I'll be his Father, and he'll be My son. I won't pull My mercy from him like I did with the one before you.'
17.14: 'His spot in My house and My kingdom? That's permanent. His throne? Locked in forever.'"'
17.15: Nathan told David every single word of that vision, just like God gave it to him.
17.16: Then King David went in, sat before the Lord, and said, 'Who am I, Lord God? And how'd my family even get this far?'
17.17: 'And on top of that, You talkin' like You got long-term plans for my people? You really treatin' me like royalty, Lord.'
17.18: 'What more can I even say? You know me inside and out. You know what I'm about.'
17.19: 'Lord, You did all this outta love for Your servant, and You chose to show off Your greatness to me.'
17.20: 'There ain't nobody like You, Lord. No other god out here compares. We done heard all this with our own ears.'
17.21: 'And who else got a people like Israel? A whole nation You stepped in to redeem for Yourself—to make Your name famous, to do wild, powerful things by takin' out nations ahead of Your people, the ones You rescued from Egypt.'
17.22: 'You made Israel Your people forever, and You, Lord, became their God.'
17.23: 'So now, Lord, everything You promised about me and my house? Make it official. Do what You said.'
17.24: 'Let it stand, and let Your name shine forever. Let folks say, "The Lord of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, is really Israel's God!" And let my house stay planted right in front of You.'
17.25: 'You, my God, let me in on the plan. You said You'd build me a house. That's why I got bold enough to pray like this.'
17.26: 'Lord, You are God. And You said You'd bless me with all this goodness.'
17.27: 'Now that You done blessed my house, it's gon' stay blessed forever—'cause when You bless somethin', it's permanent, Lord.'

18.1: After all that, David ran up on the Philistines, beat 'em down, and took Gath plus all the towns around it from their hands.
18.2: Then he handled Moab too. After that, the Moabites had to fall in line and bring him tribute—they was basically payin' taxes now.
18.3: David also smashed Hadadezer, king of Zobah, all the way to Hamath. That dude was tryna flex power near the Euphrates, but David wasn't havin' it.
18.4: He took 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. David crippled most of the horses so they couldn't be used in battle, but kept just enough for 100 chariots.
18.5: Then the Syrians from Damascus tried to back Hadadezer up—but David wiped out 22,000 of 'em.
18.6: After that, David set up military posts in Syria of Damascus. They had to fall in line too and bring him tribute. Wherever David went, God had his back.
18.7: David took all the gold shields from Hadadezer's crew and brought them back to Jerusalem.
18.8: From the cities of Tibhath and Chun (Hadadezer's territory), he took a whole lot of bronze. Later, Solomon used that to make the giant bronze Sea, pillars, and other temple pieces.
18.9: When Tou, king of Hamath, heard David had crushed Hadadezer's army, he knew what time it was.
18.10: So he sent his son Hadoram to salute King David and show love—'cause Hadadezer had been beefin' with Tou too. Hadoram came with all kinds of gold, silver, and bronze as gifts.
18.11: David didn't keep that for himself. He dedicated it all to the Lord—just like the silver and gold he got from Edom, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, and Amalek.
18.12: Meanwhile, Abishai (son of Zeruiah) took out 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Straight dominance.
18.13: He also set up garrisons in Edom, and they had to submit too. The whole country was servin' David. And again—God kept coverin' him everywhere he went.
18.14: David ruled over all Israel, and he kept things just—handlin' court cases and makin' sure things were fair for the people.
18.15: Joab (Zeruiah's son) was the commander of the army. Jehoshaphat (son of Ahilud) handled the records.
18.16: Zadok (son of Ahitub) and Abimelech (son of Abiathar) were the priests. Shavsha was the scribe.
18.17: Benaiah (son of Jehoiada) was over the Cherethites and Pelethites (David's elite guards), and David's own sons were high-ranking officials right beside him.

19.1: So after that, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, and his son Hanun took the throne.
19.2: David was like, 'I'ma show Hanun some love, since his pops showed me love.' So he sent his people to comfort Hanun after his father passed.
19.3: But the Ammonite princes got in Hanun's ear, like, 'You really think David sent them outta kindness? Man, they spies. They scoping out the land so he can take over.'
19.4: So Hanun disrespected David's crew—shaved their beards off, cut their robes at the booty, and sent them off lookin' crazy.
19.5: Word got back to David, and he sent folks to check on his guys, 'cause they were mad embarrassed. David told 'em, 'Stay at Jericho 'til your beards grow back. Then come home.'
19.6: When the Ammonites realized they messed up and were now on David's hit list, they dropped a whole bag—1,000 talents of silver—to hire help. They brought in chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Syrian Maacah, and Zobah.
19.7: They hired 32,000 chariots, plus the king of Maacah and his army. They all rolled up and camped at Medeba. The Ammonites rolled deep too, leavin' their cities and lining up for battle.
19.8: David heard about it and sent Joab and the whole squad of mighty warriors.
19.9: The Ammonites pulled up and set up right in front of their city gate. The backup kings they hired were out posted in the field.
19.10: When Joab saw he was about to get flanked—enemies in front and behind—he took the elite squad and faced off against the Syrians.
19.11: He gave the rest of the troops to his brother Abishai, who squared up against the Ammonites.
19.12: Joab told him, 'If the Syrians got me stressed, you help me. If the Ammonites start doin' the most, I got you.'
19.13: 'Let's stay solid and ride hard for our people and our cities. Let God handle the rest however He sees fit.'
19.14: Joab and his team stepped up to the Syrians—and they folded, ran off quick.
19.15: When the Ammonites saw their backup flee, they got scared too, dipped back into the city. So Joab took his crew back to Jerusalem.
19.16: When the Syrians realized Israel had worked them, they brought reinforcements from across the river. Shophach, commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.
19.17: David got the memo, pulled together all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and set up battle lines. He was ready.
19.18: When the fight popped off, the Syrians ran again. David killed 7,000 chariot riders and 40,000 foot soldiers. He even took out Shophach, their top general.
19.19: After that loss, Hadadezer's people said, 'Yeah nah, we done.' They made peace with David and became his servants. And the Syrians? They weren't messin' with the Ammonites no more after that.

20.1: It was spring—aka battle season—and Joab led the troops out to wreck Ammonite territory. He rolled up on Rabbah and laid siege to the city. David? He stayed back in Jerusalem. But Joab handled it—he took Rabbah down.
20.2: David came through later, took the crown off the Ammonite king's head—it was heavy, like a whole talent of gold, with precious gems in it. David wore it himself. Then they looted the whole city—took everything valuable.
20.3: He rounded up all the people in the city and put 'em to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He did the same to every Ammonite city he took. After that, David and the squad headed back to Jerusalem.
20.4: Later, another fight popped off with the Philistines at Gezer. Sibbechai the Hushathite stepped up and killed Sippai, one of the giant's sons. The Philistines had to fall back.
20.5: Another battle broke out, and Elhanan (Jair's son) killed Lahmi, Goliath's brother. Lahmi had a spear shaft thick like a weaver's beam—big dude, but he still got dropped.
20.6: Then another war went down in Gath. There was this dude—huge—six fingers on each hand, six toes on each foot. Twenty-four digits total. He was born from the same giant bloodline.
20.7: He dared to talk trash to Israel, so Jonathan, son of Shimea (David's brother), stepped up and handled him.
20.8: All of these were giant blood from Gath, but they all got taken out by David and his crew.

21.1: Then Satan got in the mix and pushed David to take a census of Israel.
21.2: So David told Joab and the leaders, 'Go count everybody in Israel—from Beersheba to Dan—and bring me the numbers. I wanna know what we workin' with.'
21.3: But Joab pushed back, like, 'May the Lord bless us with a hundred times more people! But my king, ain't they all your people already? Why you tryna do this? It could bring guilt on Israel.'
21.4: But David wasn't tryin' to hear it. He overruled Joab. So Joab did what he was told—traveled all through Israel, then came back to Jerusalem.
21.5: He gave David the headcount: 1.1 million sword-ready soldiers from Israel and 470,000 from Judah.
21.6: But Joab didn't count Levi and Benjamin—he hated this command so much he couldn't bring himself to finish it.
21.7: God wasn't feelin' this move at all. He brought judgment on Israel.
21.8: David cried out, 'God, I messed up bad. That was on me. Please forgive me for doin' such a foolish thing.'
21.9: Then the Lord spoke to Gad, David's prophet.
21.10: 'Go tell David: This is what the Lord says—You got three options. Pick one, and I'll make it happen.'
21.11: Gad came to David and said, 'Here's the Lord's word—
21.12: 'You can choose: three years of famine, or three months gettin' chased down and beat by your enemies, or three days of the Lord's plague across the land—with His angel bringin' destruction. Think it over and let me know what to tell Him.'
21.13: David said, 'Man, I'm torn up. But let me fall into the hands of God, not humans. He's way more merciful.'
21.14: So the Lord sent a plague over Israel. Seventy thousand men died, just like that.
21.15: God even sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But then He pulled back and said, 'That's enough. Stop now.' The angel of the Lord was standin' by Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor.
21.16: David looked up and saw the angel hoverin' between heaven and earth, sword drawn over Jerusalem. He and the elders fell on their faces, rockin' sackcloth in full sorrow.
21.17: David said, 'Lord, this was all me. I'm the one who sinned and called for the census. But these folks—Your people—they didn't do nothin'. Punish me and my family, but not them.'
21.18: Then the angel told Gad to tell David to go build an altar on Ornan's threshing floor.
21.19: So David went, just like God told him through Gad.
21.20: Ornan was out there workin' the wheat when he looked up and saw the angel. His four sons ran and hid, but he kept on workin'.
21.21: When David rolled up, Ornan saw him and dropped to the ground face-first.
21.22: David said, 'Let me buy this threshing floor so I can build an altar to the Lord and stop the plague. I'll pay full price.'
21.23: But Ornan said, 'Nah, my king—take it! Do whatever you need. I'll even give you the oxen for offerings, the tools for wood, and the wheat. It's all yours.'
21.24: But David said, 'Nope. I'm payin' full price. I ain't givin' God a sacrifice that didn't cost me nothin.'
21.25: So David paid Ornan 600 gold shekels for the spot.
21.26: David built an altar there, gave burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on the Lord. God answered with fire from heaven that hit the altar.
21.27: Then the Lord told the angel to chill, and the angel put the sword back in its sheath.
21.28: When David saw God responded to him at Ornan's place, he kept worshipin' right there.
21.29: At that time, the Lord's tabernacle and Moses' altar were still set up at the high place in Gibeon.
21.30: But David couldn't bring himself to go there—he was shook by that angel and his sword.

22.1: David said, 'This right here—that's the spot for the Lord's house. And that altar? That's where Israel gon' bring the burnt offerings.'
22.2: He called together all the foreigners livin' in Israel and put them to work. He assigned masons to start cuttin' stones for the Lord's temple.
22.3: David stacked up iron for the door nails and the joints, plus a whole heap of bronze too—so much they couldn't even measure it.
22.4: He also stocked up on cedar wood, 'cause the folks from Sidon and Tyre brought a lot of it for him.
22.5: David said, 'Look, Solomon's still young and green, and this house for the Lord gotta be next-level—world famous, straight glory. I'mma do all the prep now.' So David went all in before he died.
22.6: Then David called his son Solomon and gave him the mission—to build a house for the Lord God of Israel.
22.7: He told him, 'Son, I had it in my heart to build a house for God's name.'
22.8: 'But God told me straight up: "You done shed too much blood, fought too many wars. You not the one to build My house—you done got too much blood on your hands."'
22.9: 'But you gon' have a son. He'll be a man of peace, and I'll give him rest from all his enemies. His name gon' be Solomon, and I'ma bring peace and quiet in his time.'
22.10: 'He the one who gon' build My house. I'ma treat him like a son, and he'll be My child. His throne over Israel? I'ma make that forever.'
22.11: 'So now, my son—may the Lord be with you. Walk in what He told you, and build that house for the Lord your God.'
22.12: 'And I pray He give you wisdom and understanding as you lead Israel. Follow God's laws and don't stray.'
22.13: 'You'll succeed if you stay on point with everything the Lord told Moses about Israel. Stay strong. Don't be scared. Don't fall apart.'
22.14: 'Look, I went hard preparing for this—I saved up 100,000 talents of gold, a million talents of silver, and way too much bronze and iron to count. Got you timber and stone too, and you can add more if needed.'
22.15: 'You got workers on deck—woodcutters, stonemasons, and skilled craftsmen of every kind.'
22.16: 'Ain't no shortage of gold, silver, bronze, or iron. So get up, get to work. And may the Lord roll with you while you do it.'
22.17: Then David told all the leaders of Israel, 'Help my son Solomon out.'
22.18: 'Ain't the Lord your God already with y'all? Ain't He given you peace all around? He handed y'all the land and cleared out the people in front of us—y'all know it's God's doing.'
22.19: 'So now, lock in. Chase after the Lord with everything you got. It's time to rise up and build His sanctuary, bring in the Ark of the Covenant, and all the holy items—set it all up in the house that's bein' built for His name.'

23.1: When David got old and was full of years, he made Solomon king over Israel.
23.2: Then he called all the leaders of Israel together, including the priests and Levites.
23.3: They counted all the Levite men age 30 and up—came out to 38,000 total.
23.4: Outta that, 24,000 were put in charge of the Lord's house work, 6,000 were set as officials and judges,
23.5: 4,000 were assigned to watch the gates, and another 4,000 were set to praise the Lord with instruments. David said, 'I made these instruments just for worship.'
23.6: David broke 'em into groups based on Levi's sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
23.7: From Gershon came Laadan and Shimei.
23.8: Laadan's sons were Jehiel (the oldest), Zetham, and Joel—three total.
23.9: Shimei's sons were Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran—also three. These were the leaders from Laadan's side.
23.10: Shimei had four more sons: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah.
23.11: Jahath was the oldest, Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah didn't have many kids, so they were grouped as one family line.
23.12: Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
23.13: Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his sons were set apart forever to handle the most sacred duties—burnin' incense, serving the Lord, and blessing the people in God's name.
23.14: Moses' sons were still counted as Levites.
23.15: Moses had two sons: Gershon and Eliezer.
23.16: From Gershon came Shebuel, his oldest.
23.17: Eliezer's son Rehabiah was the first. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's line grew large.
23.18: Izhar's son was Shelomith, his oldest.
23.19: Hebron's sons were Jeriah (first), Amariah (second), Jahaziel (third), and Jekameam (fourth).
23.21: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli had Eleazar and Kish.
23.22: Eleazar died without sons—only daughters. So Kish's sons married Eleazar's daughters to keep the line goin'.
23.23: Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three total.
23.24: These were the Levite families, listed by their father's houses—heads of the clans, individually counted by name, age 20 and up, all workin' in the service of the Lord's house.
23.25: David said, 'God has given Israel peace. The people can now settle in Jerusalem for good.'
23.26: 'And the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of its gear.'
23.27: So by David's last instruction, the Levites were now counted from age 20 and up.
23.28: Their new job was to help Aaron's descendants in the Lord's temple—serving in the courtyards and rooms, cleaning the holy items, and helpin' with the rest of the duties.
23.29: They handled the showbread, the fine flour for grain offerings, unleavened bread, baked goods, pan-fried stuff, and anything measured out.
23.30: Every morning and evening they showed up to thank and praise the Lord.
23.31: They also showed up for every burnt offering on Sabbaths, new moons, and festivals—every time, by schedule, just like the law said.
23.32: They took care of the tent of meeting, the holy place, and backed up the priests—Aaron's family—in all the work for the Lord's house.

24.1: These the breakdowns of Aaron's sons and their priestly duties. Aaron had Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
24.2: Nadab and Abihu died before their daddy and left no kids. So only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to serve as priests.
24.3: David, along with Zadok (from Eleazar's line) and Ahimelech (from Ithamar's line), set up the service schedules for them.
24.4: Turns out Eleazar's side had more clan leaders than Ithamar's—16 from Eleazar, and 8 from Ithamar.
24.5: So they split them up by casting lots—taking turns—since both families had priests working in the Lord's temple.
24.6: Shemaiah (son of Nethanel), one of the Levites, wrote everything down while King David, the leaders, Zadok, Ahimelech (son of Abiathar), and the heads of the priestly families were all present. They took one lot for Eleazar's line, one for Ithamar's, back and forth.
24.19: This was their official service schedule for goin' into the Lord's house, based on what Aaron passed down, just like the Lord commanded.
24.20: Other Levite families: from Amram's line—Shubael. From Shubael—Jehdeiah.
24.21: From Rehabiah's line—Isshiah was the first.
24.23: Hebron's line: Jeriah was first, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, Jekameam fourth.
24.25: Michah's brother Isshiah had a son named Zechariah.
24.26: From Merari's line: sons were Mahli and Mushi. From Jaaziah—Beno.
24.27: Jaaziah's sons were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
24.28: From Mahli—Eleazar, but he ain't have any sons.
24.30: Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. All these were Levite families, grouped by their fathers' houses.
24.31: They cast lots for duties too, just like the priestly families. King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and all the family heads of the priests and Levites were there. The senior men and the younger ones all got the same treatment.

25.1: David and the army commanders picked out men from Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun's families to handle music ministry. These brothas used harps, stringed instruments, and cymbals to speak God's word through song.
25.2: From Asaph's sons: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. They were under their father Asaph's lead, who followed the king's direction while prophesyin' in music.
25.3: From Jeduthun's line: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah—six sons total. They served under Jeduthun, who used a harp to give thanks and praise to the Lord.
25.4: From Heman's family: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth—14 sons in all.
25.5: These were Heman's kids—he was the king's seer, speakin' God's word through song. God blessed him with 14 sons and 3 daughters to raise the horn of praise.
25.6: All of them served under their fathers in the music ministry at the Lord's house, using cymbals, harps, and strings. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman were under the king's authority.
25.7: There were 288 trained musicians in total—experts in songs for the Lord. Every one of them was skilled.
25.8: They cast lots for their rotation, no matter if they were a vet or just startin' out—everybody got their shot.
25.9: The first lot went to Joseph. Second to Gedaliah, along with his sons and brothers—12 in all.
25.10: Third lot: Zaccur and his crew—12 total.
25.11: Fourth: Jizri and his fam—12 strong.
25.12: Fifth: Nethaniah, with 12 of his own.
25.14: Seventh: Jesharelah and his people—12 deep.
25.17: Tenth: Shimei and 12 of his folk.
25.20: Thirteenth: Shubael and his group of 12.
25.24: Seventeenth: Joshbekashah and 12 in his squad.
25.26: Nineteenth: Mallothi and twelve with him.
25.27: Twentieth: Eliathah and his crew of 12.
25.29: Twenty-second: Giddalti and 12 under his name.
25.30: Twenty-third: Mahazioth with 12 in his crew.
25.31: Twenty-fourth: Romamti-Ezer—him and his 12 were the final squad on rotation.

26.1: The gatekeeper squads were organized too. From the Korahite fam, Meshelemiah (son of Kore, from Asaph's line) was posted up.
26.2: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah (firstborn), Jediael (second), Zebadiah (third), Jathniel (fourth),
26.4: Obed-Edom's sons were: Shemaiah (first), Jehozabad (second), Joah (third), Sacar (fourth), Nethanel (fifth),
26.5: Ammiel (sixth), Issachar (seventh), and Peulthai (eighth)—God had blessed his whole fam.
26.6: Shemaiah, Obed-Edom's son, also had sons. They ran their family biz strong, 'cause they were some real ones—solid and wise.
26.7: His boys were Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad—and his brothers Elihu and Semachiah—dudes with skill.
26.8: Everybody in Obed-Edom's crew—sons and brothers—were strong and dependable. Sixty-two men deep.
26.9: Meshelemiah had 18 sons and brothers who could handle the job.
26.10: Hosah (from Merari's people) had sons too. Shimri got made the first, even though he wasn't born first—his dad put him in charge anyway.
26.11: Then came Hilkiah (second), Tebaliah (third), and Zechariah (fourth). Hosah had 13 sons and brothers in total.
26.12: These were the leaders of the gatekeeper groups. They all had jobs to do, just like the rest of the Levites, workin' in the Lord's house.
26.13: They cast lots to see who got posted at which gate—no favoritism, whether they were high or low rank.
26.14: East Gate: Shelemiah. North Gate: his son Zechariah (called a wise advisor).
26.15: South Gate: Obed-Edom. His sons handled the storage rooms.
26.16: West Gate: Shuppim and Hosah. Plus they got the Shallecheth Gate on the hill road—Levites watchin' both sides.
26.17: Each day: six Levites on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two by two at the storehouse.
26.18: At the Parbar (western complex): four on the road, two more by the building.
26.19: These were the gatekeeper squads from the Korahite and Merarite lines.
26.20: Ahijah (a Levite) managed the treasuries for the Lord's house, including sacred items.
26.21: From Laadan's family (descended from Gershon), the lead guy was Jehieli.
26.22: His sons Zetham and Joel ran the temple's treasure storage.
26.23: More Levites handled sacred duties too: the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites.
26.24: Shebuel (Moses' grandson from Gershom's line) was the top boss over all treasuries.
26.25: His extended fam—Eliezer's descendants: Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomith.
