26.26: Shelomith and his people oversaw everything David and the army leaders had dedicated to the Lord's house.
26.27: Some of that came from battle spoils they set aside to support temple upkeep.
26.28: Everything Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab had dedicated to God was also managed by Shelomith and his crew.
26.29: Chenaniah and his sons (from the Izharite line) were officers and judges handling affairs outside Jerusalem.
26.30: Hashabiah and his brothers (1,700 Hebronites) had the job of managing all the Lord's business—and the king's—west of the Jordan.
26.31: Jerijah was the head of the Hebronites. In David's 40th year as king, they searched the family records and found capable men in Jazer, Gilead.
26.32: They found 2,700 more qualified heads of households, and David appointed them to handle responsibilities for the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. They managed everything tied to God and the king.

27.1: Israel's army was organized by family leaders, captains of thousands and hundreds, and their officers. Each group took turns servin' the king—one division per month, twelve months total. Each division had 24,000 soldiers.
27.2: January squad (first month) was led by Jashobeam, son of Zabdiel. His group had 24,000 men.
27.3: He came from the family line of Perez and was top dog over all the first-month troops.
27.4: February squad (second month) had Dodai the Ahohite in charge. Mikloth helped lead. His group had 24,000.
27.5: March squad (third month) was under Benaiah, son of Jehoiada the priest. He was the chief. His division also had 24,000.
27.6: This Benaiah was one of the mighty thirty and led them too. His son Ammizabad was part of his squad.
27.7: April squad (fourth month) was led by Asahel (Joab's brother), then by Asahel's son Zebadiah after him. Same—24,000 men.
27.8: May squad (fifth month): Shamhuth the Izrahite. Another 24,000 deep.
27.9: June squad (sixth month): Ira, son of Ikkesh from Tekoa. 24,000 soldiers.
27.10: July squad (seventh month): Helez the Pelonite from Ephraim's tribe. Had 24,000 too.
27.11: August squad (eighth month): Sibbechai the Hushathite from the Zarhites. 24,000.
27.12: September squad (ninth month): Abiezer from Anathoth in Benjamin's tribe. 24,000.
27.13: October squad (tenth month): Maharai the Netophathite from the Zarhites. 24,000.
27.14: November squad (eleventh month): Benaiah the Pirathonite from Ephraim's tribe. 24,000 soldiers.
27.15: December squad (twelfth month): Heldai the Netophathite from Othniel's clan. 24,000 as well.
27.16: These were the tribal officers: Reuben: Eliezer, son of Zichri Simeon: Shephatiah, son of Maachah
27.17: Levi: Hashabiah, son of Kemuel Aaron's family: Zadok
27.18: Judah: Elihu, one of David's brothers Issachar: Omri, son of Michael
27.19: Zebulun: Ishmaiah, son of Obadiah Naphtali: Jerimoth, son of Azriel
27.20: Ephraim: Hoshea, son of Azaziah Half-tribe of Manasseh: Joel, son of Pedaiah
27.21: Other half of Manasseh (in Gilead): Iddo, son of Zechariah Benjamin: Jaasiel, son of Abner
27.22: Dan: Azarel, son of Jeroham. These were all the tribal chiefs for Israel.
27.23: David didn't count the men under 20 years old, 'cause the Lord said He'd multiply Israel like the stars.
27.24: Joab (Zeruiah's son) started the count but didn't finish, 'cause God's anger broke out over it. So the final numbers weren't even included in David's official records.
27.25: Azmaveth (son of Adiel) managed the royal treasuries. Jehonathan (son of Uzziah) handled the storage buildings in the cities, fields, villages, and fortresses.
27.26: Ezri (son of Chelub) oversaw the field workers.
27.27: Shimei from Ramah ran the vineyards. Zabdi from Shepham handled the wine supplies.
27.28: Baal-Hanan from Geder looked after olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands. Joash was over the oil storage.
27.29: Shitrai from Sharon took care of the herds in that region. Shaphat (son of Adlai) handled the valley herds.
27.30: Obil the Ishmaelite ran the camels. Jehdeiah from Meronoth was over the donkeys.
27.31: Jaziz the Hagrite handled the flocks. All these were the officials who managed King David's assets.
27.32: David's uncle Jehonathan was a wise counselor and scribe. Jehiel (son of Hachmoni) mentored the king's sons.
27.33: Ahithophel was David's top advisor. Hushai the Archite was his close companion.
27.34: After Ahithophel came Jehoiada (son of Benaiah), then Abiathar. And Joab was still the commander of the whole army.

28.1: David called a big meetin' in Jerusalem. He gathered all the leaders of Israel—tribal officials, army captains over thousands and hundreds, those who managed the king's stuff and his sons' properties, top officials, warriors, and mighty men.
28.2: Then King David stood up and said, 'Listen up, my people. I had it on my heart to build a resting place for the Ark of God's covenant—somewhere fitting for His footstool. I even got everything ready to do it.'
28.3: 'But God told me, "You ain't the one to build My house. You've been in too many wars, spilled too much blood."'
28.4: 'Still, the Lord, God of Israel, chose me—outta my whole family line—to be king over Israel forever. He picked Judah to rule, picked my dad's family from Judah, and then He chose me from among my brothers to be king.'
28.5: 'And outta all my sons (and trust, the Lord gave me plenty), He picked Solomon to sit on the throne of the Lord's kingdom over Israel.'
28.6: 'God told me, "Solomon your son is the one who'll build My house and My courtyards. I picked him to be My son, and I'ma be his Father."'
28.7: '"If he stays faithful to My commands and listens like he should, I'll lock in his kingdom forever."'
28.8: 'So now, in front of all Israel, and before God, make sure y'all keep His commandments. Do what He says so you can keep this land and pass it on to your children forever.'
28.9: 'And you, my son Solomon—get to know the God of your father. Serve Him with all your heart and with a willing mind. He sees the real you. He knows your thoughts before you think 'em. If you seek Him, you'll find Him. But if you walk away, He'll leave you behind.'
28.10: 'So take this serious. God chose you to build His sanctuary. Be strong, and get it done.'
28.11: Then David handed Solomon the full blueprint: the entrance, the rooms, the treasuries, the upstairs rooms, the inner spaces, and the spot for the mercy seat.
28.12: He gave him plans that came straight from the Spirit—how to lay out the temple courts, the rooms around them, the storage for sacred things, and the special treasuries.
28.13: He included instructions for organizing the priests and Levites, all the service jobs in the Lord's house, and all the items they'd use in worship.
28.14: He even gave specific amounts of gold for gold items and silver for silver items—down to the last detail for every single task.
28.15: Gold for each gold lampstand and its lamps, and silver for each silver one—everything was laid out by how it was supposed to be used.
28.16: He provided gold by weight for the tables of showbread, and silver for the silver tables.
28.17: He gave pure gold for the meat forks, bowls, and pitchers. Every golden bowl had its weight marked, and the same for each silver one.
28.18: He even weighed out refined gold for the incense altar and the golden chariot—the cherubim with wings that covered the Ark of the Covenant.
28.19: David said, 'God gave me all of this. Every detail. He showed me everything in writing—this was His hand on me.'
28.20: Then David said to Solomon, 'Be strong. Be bold. And do it. Don't be scared or discouraged, 'cause the Lord—my God—He's with you. He ain't goin' nowhere 'til you finish everything for the Lord's house.'
28.21: 'You got all the priests and Levites set for service. Skilled workers ready to handle all kinds of craftsmanship. Plus the leaders and the people—they all got your back.'

29.1: Then King David told everybody, 'Look, my son Solomon—God's chosen him, but he still young and new to all this. And this job? It's major. We ain't just buildin' a building for folks—it's for the Lord God Himself.'
29.2: So I gave everything I had for God's house—gold for gold stuff, silver for silver things, bronze for bronze work, iron, wood, onyx, decorative stones, colorful gems, precious stones, marble—everything in bulk.
29.3: And because I love God's house, I'm givin' even more from my own stash—my personal treasure of gold and silver—on top of all I already set aside.
29.4: I'm givin' 3,000 talents of gold (from Ophir!) and 7,000 talents of refined silver just to cover the temple walls.
29.5: Gold for gold work, silver for silver work—all for the craftsmen doin' their thing. So… who else ridin' with me? Who gon' dedicate themselves to the Lord today?
29.6: Then the leaders of the clans, the tribal chiefs, army commanders, and officials in charge of the king's work stepped up and gave willingly.
29.7: They gave 5,000 talents and 10,000 darics of gold, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.
29.8: And those who had gems gave 'em straight to the treasury of the Lord's house, handled by Jehiel the Gershonite.
29.9: The people were hype—they gave from the heart. King David saw it and couldn't stop smilin'—he was mad joyful.
29.10: David praised the Lord in front of everybody, sayin': 'Blessed are You, Lord God of Israel, our Father, forever and ever.'
29.11: 'Yours, Lord, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, the majesty. Everything in heaven and earth belongs to You. The kingdom is Yours, Lord, and You sit high above all.'
29.12: 'Wealth and honor? That's all from You. You're the one in charge. You lift folks up, You give strength.'
29.13: 'So now, God, we thank You and lift up Your holy name.'
29.14: 'But really—who am I? Who are we, Lord, that we could even give like this? Everything we got came from You. We just givin' back what's already Yours.'
29.15: 'We're just visitors here—travelers. Just like our ancestors. Our time on earth is short—like a shadow. And we ain't even in control of it.'
29.16: 'Lord, all this stuff we've gathered to build Your house came from You. It's Yours anyway.'
29.17: 'I know You test hearts and love uprightness. I gave all this freely and joyfully. And I see Your people here, givin' with that same joy.'
29.18: 'Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel—keep this spirit in Your people forever. Keep their hearts turned toward You.'
29.19: 'Give my son Solomon a heart that sticks with You. Help him follow Your commands and build the temple I prepped for.'
29.20: Then David told the crowd, 'Let's bless the Lord, y'all.' And everybody bowed down and worshipped the Lord and honored the king.
29.21: The next day they made sacrifices—1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs—plus drink offerings and more sacrifices. Israel turned up in praise.
29.22: They ate and drank in God's presence with joy. And they made Solomon king again, anointin' him as leader before the Lord and anointin' Zadok as priest.
29.23: Solomon sat on the Lord's throne, takin' his father David's place as king. He was blessed and backed by all Israel.
29.24: All the leaders, mighty men, and David's sons bowed down and pledged loyalty to Solomon.
29.25: The Lord made Solomon look real royal—next-level glory that no king before him in Israel had ever seen.
29.26: That's how David, son of Jesse, ruled all Israel.
29.27: He reigned 40 years—7 in Hebron, 33 in Jerusalem.
29.28: David died old and full of years, blessings, and respect. And Solomon took the throne.
29.29: Everything David did—from the beginning to the end—is written in the books of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer.
29.30: That includes his whole reign, his power moves, and all that went down in Israel and the neighboring kingdoms.
